label: GO-only a2 preference: ideal-observer belief S2 good, plus last-trial pattern
terms: (phase == GO) * np.tanh(-belief_lo) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u")
explanation: Fires only at GO (D1/D2 essentially zero). Magnitude tracks how strongly an ideal observer believes S2 is the good state: a saturating tanh(-belief_lo) term is the main driver (GO residual runs from about +2.2 at belief decile 0 to -2.0 at decile 9). On top of that, a previous a2 choice raises it, and the last-trial pattern shifts it in the model-based direction: after a1 S1 u it drops strongly, after a1 S2 r and a1 S2 u it drops, after a2 S1 r it rises. belief_cover and the trial-before choice add <0.01. Observed-only test R^2 beyond timing 0.786 (dev 0.803), versus 0.90 for the model policy-decile reference and 0.88 for the all-observed table ceiling (all = 0.94), so leaving out the model outputs costs roughly 0.1. No future variables are used.

issues: The numbers reproduce. The claimed 6 terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.786. The GO-only claim holds: the D1 and D2 residuals are about 1e-5. The belief-decile residuals (+2.24 down to -1.98) and the term signs also match (weights: tanh +1.61, prev a2 +0.45, a1S1u -1.36, a1S2r -0.82, a2S1r +0.68, a1S2u -0.47). Adding belief_cover (<10) changed R^2 by <0.001, and the choice two trials back by <0.005, so 'gained <0.01' is correct.

The explanation says the last-trial effects shift the feature 'in the model-based direction'. Two of them clearly do not. a2 S1 r (rare rewarded) raises this a2 feature (+0.68), but a model-based agent should switch to a1 there, so a rise is the model-free direction: repeat the rewarded action. a1 S2 r lowers the a2 feature (-0.82), which is again model-free (repeat a1 after reward); model-based would favour a2. a1 S1 u (common unrewarded) drops strongly (-1.36), where both model-based and model-free switching would raise a2, so beyond belief it looks perseverative. On top of the ideal-observer belief, the residual history effects are reward-driven repetition of the last action plus perseveration, not model-based.

The belief shape is too smooth. The decile residuals step sharply between deciles 3 and 5 (+1.51, +0.42, -1.02). Adding a cubic tanh(-belief_lo)**3, or a second, sharper tanh(-2*belief_lo), lifts test R^2 from 0.786 to 0.80-0.805 with no other change.

A gap to the all-observed ceiling remains (0.88, against 0.786-0.805), and I could not close it within 8 terms. A full last-trial table plus belief gives 0.788, and two-trials-back choice terms add <0.01. In the worst-fit windows the feature is 0 at GO even though belief strongly favours S2 and the agent keeps choosing a2 (predicted ~4, actual 0). The errors grouped by phase x previous trial are small (largest -0.2 to -0.3, after a2 S1 u or a1 S2 u), so this is not one large systematic class, but the observed-only account is roughly 0.08-0.1 short of both the table ceiling and the model-policy reference (0.90).
